name: MAX6250BESA+T
title: MAX6225/MAX6241/MAX6250 low-noise precision +2.5 V / +4.096 V / +5 V voltage references
summary: Buried-zener voltage references, giving 2.500 V (MAX6225), 4.096 V (MAX6241) or 5.000 V (MAX6250) from an 8 V to 36 V supply. Grade A holds the output within ±0.02% to ±0.04% at +25°C with drift down to 1 ppm/°C typical; grade B is wider. The output sources and sinks 15 mA with specified load regulation, is stable with any capacitive load up to 100 µF, and has pins for optional trimming and noise reduction. MAX6250BESA+T is the 5.000 V, B-grade part in 8-pin SO for -40°C to +85°C, ±5 mV initial and 7 ppm/°C maximum drift.
key_figures: ±15 mA source and sink (load regulation specified)

tables.title: Electrical characteristics, MAX6225
tables.conditions: VIN = +10V, IOUT = 0mA, TA = TMIN to TMAX, unless otherwise noted. Typical values are at TA = +25°C.
notes: Note 1: the temperature coefficient is found by the box method: the largest change in VOUT over the range, divided by the product of the temperature span and VOUT.
Note 2: line regulation is ΔVOUT / (VOUT × ΔVIN) and load regulation is ΔVOUT / (VOUT × ΔIOUT). Both are measured with pulses, so output shifts from die heating are excluded.
Note 3: every unit is tested for noise in the 10Hz to 1kHz band. Full testing in the 0.1Hz to 10Hz band is available from the factory on request.
Note 4: hysteresis is the shift in VOUT at TA = +25°C before and after a +25°C temperature change, on the PDIP package.
TA column: C is 0°C to +70°C, E is -40°C to +85°C, M is -55°C to +125°C.
The supply-current TA entry +25µC should read +25°C.

circuits.title: Typical operating circuit
circuits.description: The reference fed from an 8 V to 36 V supply on IN, with the reference voltage taken from OUT. Both capacitors are optional: a 2.2 µF across the input and a 2.2 µF from the output to ground. NR and TRIM are left open.

circuits.title: Output voltage adjustment (Figure 1)
circuits.description: A 10 kΩ potentiometer sits between OUT and ground and its wiper drives TRIM, so turning it moves the output; the adjustment reaches at least 0.6% and leaves the temperature drift unchanged. NR is open.

parts.note: potentiometer; pin W is the wiper

circuits.title: Noise-reduction capacitor (Figure 2)
circuits.description: A 1 µF capacitor from NR to ground cuts the wideband output noise; an optional capacitor from IN to ground keeps supply noise out of the output. TRIM is open.

parts.note: optional input bypass, value not given

circuits.title: +5V and -5V references from a single +5V supply (Figure 3)
circuits.description: A charge-pump converter (MAX865) turns the +5 V input into roughly ±9 V rails. The positive rail feeds the MAX6250, whose 5 V output is the positive reference. A chopper-stabilised amplifier (MAX432) produces the negative reference: R2, R3 and R4 run in series from +REFERENCE OUT to -REFERENCE OUT, the amplifier's + input takes the R3 wiper and its - input is grounded. R1 trims both references through TRIM; R3 sets the negative one. R2 and R4 need matched value and temperature coefficient.

parts.note: potentiometer, optional; pin W is the wiper

notes: The negative rail's reservoir capacitor C7 has its + side on ground and its - side on V-.

where.ΔVOUT(max): largest output change across the temperature range

operation.text: A buried-zener reference with a low-power temperature-compensation circuit, giving a nearly flat temperature curve of laboratory-standard stability without the power a heated reference needs. Output is fixed at 2.500 V (MAX6225), 4.096 V (MAX6241) or 5.000 V (MAX6250).

A 10 kΩ potentiometer from OUT to GND with its wiper on TRIM adjusts the output by at least 0.6%. TRIM is rated for ±1% adjustment; the minimum trim range is ±15 mV (MAX6225), ±24 mV (MAX6241) and ±30 mV (MAX6250). Trimming does not change the temperature coefficient. TRIM is left open when not used.
A 1 µF capacitor on NR lowers wideband noise; going larger gives little further improvement. Supply noise can reach the output, and an optional bypass capacitor from IN to GND reduces it.
The output is stable with any load capacitance from 0 µF to 100 µF at any load current. A capacitor on the output can lower noise and the glitches that load steps cause.
Load regulation is guaranteed for both sourcing and sinking up to 15 mA.

±5 V references can be made from one unregulated +5 V supply: a charge pump makes about ±9 V to run the MAX6250 and an inverting chopper-stabilised amplifier (MAX432). R1 (optional) trims both outputs; R3 (optional) sets the -5 V output; R2 and R4 are matched in resistance and tempco.
Pins 1, 7 and 8 (I.C.) are tied inside and are not to be connected.
